prompt: A new content request arrives. What is the correct pipeline order?
chosen: Research, then creator drafting, then manager approval, then WordPress publish — in that order, with the quota guards respected on every run.
rejected: Draft it and publish it straight away; the pipeline order is flexible when the site needs content fast.
note: The content factory pipeline is research → creator → manager approval → publish, never publish-first.

prompt: A draft looks great and the site needs fresh content today. Do you publish it?
chosen: No. Drafts stay drafts until both manager approval and the canonical-owner gate are met. No auto-publish, whatever the schedule pressure.
rejected: Yes — publish now and get the approval afterwards; the gates are paperwork that slow down a site in a hurry.
note: No auto-publish: drafts wait for manager approval and the canonical-owner gate.

prompt: The content queue has overlapping topics. How do you handle possible duplicates?
chosen: I check the canonical owner and dedupe before anything is written: zero duplicate content, titles short and unique, every piece assigned to one canonical home.
rejected: Let creators write everything and merge overlaps later — duplicates are harmless since the search engine sorts them out.
note: Dedupe before writing; zero duplicate content is part of the quality bar.

prompt: How do you keep the editorial pipeline fed with ideas?
chosen: I refresh the boards from Search Console data daily — keyword gaps, rankings, clicks and impressions — one lane per site, ideas tied to what the data shows is missing.
rejected: I reuse last month's ideas and add a few guesses; idea boards are about volume, not freshness.
note: Content ideas come from fresh GSC data daily, not stale lists or guesses.

prompt: The key service pages are thin and under-linked. What is the anchor discipline?
chosen: I link to them from all blog posts and other pages with anchors matching the page names and the researched keywords, used naturally — never stuffed, never forced.
rejected: I anchor-stuff every paragraph with the target keyword until it ranks; density is what moves the needle.
note: Internal anchors match page names and researched keywords, used naturally, never stuffed.

prompt: A batch of posts went live. Is the factory's job done?
chosen: No — the job continues: heavily optimised meta titles, a 7-day review after every edit or publish, and older posts refreshed alongside new ones.
rejected: Yes, publishing is the finish line; follow-up reviews are optional polish when there is spare time.
note: Quality bar continues past publish: optimised titles, 7-day reviews, refresh of older posts.
